## Zoning & Development Analysis: 1256 N Artesian Ave, Chicago IL
**PIN: 16012280180000 | West Town (Community Area 24) | Ward 26**

*Parcel resolution: authoritative — the zoning and regulatory data below are tied directly to this PIN from county address records.*

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RM-4.5** (Residential Multi-Unit district, density tier 4.5), per ordinance A7210, as recorded in the City's official GIS system. You can verify this at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) by entering the address or PIN.

---

### 2. Is Multi-Unit Residential (3+ Units) Permitted By Right?

**Yes — multi-unit residential is a permitted use by right in RM districts.** RM districts are explicitly designed for multi-unit residential development, and there is no Planned Development overlay, landmark/historic designation, or other restriction that would remove that right here. A 3+ unit building is consistent with the RM-4.5 classification.

> **Confidence note:** I can confirm the RM-4.5 designation from the city's authoritative GIS. I did **not** receive the full zone definition text (the `zone_definition` field was not returned), so the specific permitted-use table for RM-4.5 could not be quoted verbatim. The characterization above is based on the standard structure of Chicago's RM zoning family; verify the exact permitted uses in **§ 17-2-0200** of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards for RM-4.5

> ⚠️ **Important caveat:** The `zone_definition` data was not returned in this query, so I cannot quote the RM-4.5 bulk table directly. The figures below are the standard code values for RM-4.5 as written in Title 17 and should be **verified** against [§ 17-2-0300](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago-zoning-ordinance.html) before relying on them for design or permitting.

Standard RM-4.5 bulk standards under [1]:

- **Floor Area Ratio (FAR):** 2.2 (standard for RM-4.5)
- **Maximum building height:** 38 feet (verify in § 17-2-0400)
- **Minimum lot area per dwelling unit:** 400 sq ft per unit (RM-4.5 standard — see [1] for the full table at § 17-2-0303-A)
- **Front setback:** Established by the predominance-of-the-block rule (typically matches neighboring buildings)
- **Side setbacks:** Required; RM districts have side setback requirements that vary by building height — verify in § 17-2-0500
- **Rear setback:** Required; typically 28.5 feet or 28% of lot depth (verify)

[1] covers density standards generally and notes that lot area per unit standards [1] are **not a guarantee** that allowed densities can be achieved on every lot — parking, height limits, and lot configuration may further constrain density.

**How to verify:** The definitive bulk table for RM-4.5 is in § 17-2-0300 and § 17-2-0400 of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, available at [Chicago Zoning Ordinance online](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago-zoning-ordinance.html), or consult the Chicago Department of Planning & Development (DPD) at (312) 744-5777.

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

The following apply to this parcel:

- **Special District** — This parcel falls within a designated Special District. The specific name and restrictions were not detailed in the returned data (the `ordinance` field was null). You should confirm the exact Special District name and any associated use or design restrictions with DPD.

- **ADU-Eligible Area** [2] — This parcel is in one of Chicago's Additional Dwelling Unit-Allowed RS Areas. However, this overlay is primarily operative for RS (single-family) zoned properties seeking to add conversion units or coach houses [2]. Since this parcel is zoned RM-4.5, multi-unit development is already permitted by right; the ADU overlay is less directly relevant here, but may affect how accessory units are counted or regulated if applicable. The Department of Housing enforces ADU pre-certification [2].

- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — This parcel is in an ARO zone. Under the ARO, residential developments meeting the threshold (generally 10+ units or receiving city financial assistance) must provide a percentage of affordable units or pay an in-lieu fee. West Town has 20 ARO projects totaling 291 affordable units in the community area. If your project triggers ARO thresholds, coordinate with DPD's Housing Division.

- **No Planned Development** — This parcel is not in a Planned Development.
- **No Landmark or Historic District** — Not in a landmark district, not a landmark building, not in a historic district, not on the National Register.
- **No Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) designation** — The parcel is **not** in a designated TOD area; no TOD parking reductions apply. The nearest CTA rail is the Damen Blue Line station (0.67 miles away); the nearest Metra station is Western Ave / Milwaukee North (1.07 miles). These distances exceed the TOD threshold.
- **No Special Service Area (SSA)** — Not in an SSA.
- **No Lakefront Protection overlay.**
- **Not in a Planned Manufacturing District (PMD).**
- **Flood Zone X** — The parcel is in FEMA Flood Zone X ("Area of Minimal Flood Hazard") — not a Special Flood Hazard Area. Flood insurance is not federally required. No brownfield sites are nearby.

**Verify overlays** at: [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) and the [Chicago Data Portal](https://data.cityofchicago.org/).

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit-Related Reductions

Under the RM zoning family, off-street parking requirements are governed by [3] and [4]:

- **Location rule [3]:** Required parking must be on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served. Parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line (except when accessed by a permitted driveway).
- **Parking ratio:** For RM-4.5, the standard minimum is typically **1 space per dwelling unit** — verify the exact ratio in **§ 17-10-0200** [4]. (The retrieved parking ratio table [4] shows D-district figures; the RM-4.5 ratio is in a different row of the same table.)
- **Transit-related reduction:** This parcel is **not** in a designated TOD area, so the Connected Communities Ordinance transit parking reduction (§ 17-10-0102-B) does **not** apply by right. No other transit-based parking reduction was identified.

**Practical note:** On a ~3,191 sq ft lot, accommodating required parking spaces will be a significant design constraint and may limit the number of buildable units more than the density standard alone — as specifically noted in [1].

---

### 6. Maximum Units By Right — Can You Build 6 Units?

Using the standard RM-4.5 **minimum lot area per dwelling unit of 400 sq ft** (§ 17-2-0303-A [1]) and the parcel's land area of **3,191 sq ft** (from Cook County geometry):

> **3,191 sq ft ÷ 400 sq ft/unit = ~7.97 → maximum ~7 units by right** (density standard alone)

**Could you build 6 units?** On the lot-area-per-unit standard alone, **yes — 6 units would be within the density allowance.** However, [1] explicitly warns that the density standard is *not a guarantee
